enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
507 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 530 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

 - Widespread showers and thunderstorms again this afternoon and
   evening. Best chances for areas east of the Rio Grande,
   including El Paso, Hudspeth, and Otero Counties. Storms will be
   capable of large hail, damaging winds, and localized flash
   flooding.

 - Storm chances shift further east Sunday and Monday, limited
   mostly to Hudspeth and Otero Counties. A brief window of drier
   weather expected midweek before rain chances return Thursday
   into next weekend.

 - Typical late-October temperatures, with lowland highs in the
   lower to mid 70s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Deep, layered moisture continues over the CWA from the RG Valley 
east with PWs of around an inch. This could be from another upper 
trough that rotated around the upper low over SoCal. Our round of 
severe weather seemed to align with the back edge of this layered 
moisture, with convection now weakened considerably and mostly 
over Otero County. 

Saturday and Sunday...another upper trough now over western 
Arizona will rotate eastward Saturday, reaching the RG Valley mid 
afternoon. This looks to be the convective initiator, limiting 
most of the thunderstorms to the valley east starting mid 
afternoon. MUCAPES approach 1000 J/kg in the east Saturday, and 
much like today, decent speed shear with little directional shear.
Thus, some severe storms are possible again on Saturday in the 
east. Same story mostly on Sunday, though as the upper low lifts 
out over Utah and the main trough from the low moves into New 
Mexico, the convective focus may shift even a bit further east. 
The environment still keeps MUCAPES of around 500-1000 J/kg, but 
with mid level winds turning more southwest, some directional 
shear is introduced back into the area. Hail likely to be the 
biggest threat again; some flooding is possible but lower PWs and 
the continued rapid movement of the storms should keep this threat
lower. 

Monday through Wednesday...drier air at upper levels moves in as 
upper flow turns westerly. However mid level remains southerly 
Monday so slight chance of storms remains over Hudspeth/Otero 
Counties. Tuesday and Wednesday should remain dry.

Thursday and Friday...mid and upper level winds become a bit more
south/southwest as a Pacific trough approaches the west coast. 
This will draw up modest amounts of moisture, so a slight chance 
of rain will also follow for both these days. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 530 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

Widespread TS across south-central NM and W TX this evening,
likely affecting KELP and KLRU between 21-03Z. Temporary IFR VIS
due to +TSRA and gusts up to 35 knots possible. Prevailing surface
winds 150-190 at 10 to 15 knots this afternoon with skies FEW-
SCT070, SCT-BKN250. Developing CB after 20Z. Mostly dry conditions
Saturday night into Sunday morning, with lighter winds and skies
SCT-BKN120.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 530 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

Low fire danger due to recent rains. Prevailing wind out of the S
at 10 to 15 mph, with Good vent rates today. Scattered 
thunderstorms again this afternoon, affecting south-central New 
Mexico and Lincoln NF. Storms will be capable of sudden, gusty 
winds and localized flash flooding. Monday-Wednesday look drier, 
but rain chances return quickly by the end of next week. 

&&
